questions.question: You’re running late for a meeting with a client, and your colleague says, *'I’m sorry I’m late, but my car broke down on the way here.'* What would be the most appropriate response?
options: Oh, that’s terrible! I’m so sorry about that.
Don’t worry about it; you’ve got plenty of time.
You shouldn’t have taken that route—it’s much faster.
Well, at least you’re not the first person to have this problem today.
questions.answer: Oh, that’s terrible! I’m so sorry about that.

questions.question: Your friend suggests, *'Let’s go to the cinema tonight—it’s a great film opening this week.'* How would you politely respond if you’d already planned something else?
options: That sounds perfect! I’ll definitely join you.
I’m afraid I can’t—my sister is visiting me, and I’m planning to stay home.
I think it’s a brilliant idea—what time does it start?
Maybe another time, but I’m sure we’ll see that film soon.
questions.answer: I’m afraid I can’t—my sister is visiting me, and I’m planning to stay home.

questions.question: A customer at a café asks, *'Could you please bring me the bill after I’ve finished my coffee?'* What would be the most appropriate response from the café staff?
options: No, we don’t do that—you have to ask for it yourself.
Of course! I’ll bring it over right away—just take your time.
You’ll have to wait until you’re ready to leave; it’s not allowed here.
I’m sorry, we don’t serve coffee—you can try the café next door.
questions.answer: Of course! I’ll bring it over right away—just take your time.

questions.question: Your boss says to you, *'I think we should consider hiring someone with more experience in project management.'* How would you respond if you strongly disagree with this suggestion?
options: That’s a great idea! I’ll make sure to research it further.
I’m not sure that’s necessary—our current team is doing well.
I agree, but we should look at other countries first.
I think we should wait until we have more data before making a decision.
questions.answer: I’m not sure that’s necessary—our current team is doing well.

questions.question: Someone asks, *'Would you mind if I use your phone to call my mother?'* What would be the most polite and appropriate response?
options: Of course not! Here you go—just don’t take too long.
I’m sorry, I don’t have any phones here—you’ll have to ask someone else.
No, I don’t mind, but you should really use your own phone.
I’d rather you didn’t—it’s not allowed in this area.
questions.answer: Of course not! Here you go—just don’t take too long.
